newsitem.title: UK: Brent paper talked easier as wet avails pressure.
newsitem.headline: Brent paper talked easier as wet avails pressure.

text.p: Brent paper was talked a few cents easier in slow early discussion on Monday, reflecting pressure from a North Sea physical crude market awash with material, traders said.
"A number of cargoes are available and there's no arbitrage so it doesn't look good for differentials," one wet trader said.
July IPE Brent was six cents firmer at 1023 GMT but traders said early business was choppy, noting the market had dipped briefly below Friday's $17.75 close.

Benchmark Brent crude traded at a discount of 49 cents to July forward paper on Friday and short-dated swaps or CFDs were showing a value of July -53/-46 cents for the balance of this week on Monday, some three cents adrift from Friday.
The following week's CFDs were talked at July -43/37, also three cents weaker.
June 23-27 CFDs were talked at August Brent -60/-53 cents, equivalent to July 37 cents or some seven cents adrift from last week.
Intermonth spreads also showed strain. June/July was around -37/-30 cents. July August was unchanged at -25/-23 cents. August/September was three cents weaker at -23/-19 cents.
Traders said six or seven Oseberg cargoes and a similar number of Statfjords were still on the market just a few days away from the release of July loading programmes.
"Most North Sea grades are under pressure," said a broker, but he added it was unclear how many Gullfaks and Oseberg had been moved on Friday.
Two cargoes loading June 24-26 held by Exxon and Elf were due to turn wet.
